name: lan78xx_resume
prose: Resume callback of the lan78xx USB driver: takes dev->dev_mutex, and every return path releases it (single exit label out). If EVENT_DEV_OPEN is set it first calls lan78xx_flush_tx_fifo (an error jumps to out and returns that errno; EVENT_DEV_ASLEEP is then still set), resubmits dev->urb_intr when non-NULL (a failure there is only warned about, with netif_device_detach on -ENODEV, and is not returned), and under txq.lock, if the netdev is present, submits the deferred TX URBs via lan78xx_submit_deferred_urbs (which releases the buffers of URBs when the device is absent, the carrier is off or a pipe halt was already seen, and which stops the queue on -EPIPE and detaches the netdev on -ENODEV); a reported pipe halt defers EVENT_TX_HALT. It then clears EVENT_DEV_ASLEEP, starts the netdev queue only if there was no pipe halt, the device is present and the pending TX data is below the URB space, calls lan78xx_start_tx_path (an error returns that errno), schedules NAPI and, if stat_monitor is not pending, sets dev->delta = 1 and arms the timer. If EVENT_DEV_OPEN is clear it only clears EVENT_DEV_ASLEEP. In both cases it then writes the wake-up registers in order WUCSR2=0, WUCSR=0, WK_SRC=0xFFF1FF1F, WUCSR2=(NS_RCD|ARP_RCD|IPV6_TCPSYN_RCD|IPV4_TCPSYN_RCD), WUCSR=(EEE_TX_WAKE|EEE_RX_WAKE|PFDA_FR|RFE_WAKE_FR|WUFR|MPR|BCST_FR); the first write that returns a negative value ends the function with that value, otherwise the return value is 0.

name: rtl8152_check_firmware
prose: Validates a loaded Realtek r8152 firmware image (rtl_fw->fw) and returns a long: 0 on success, otherwise -EFAULT (the checksum helper also returns -EFAULT on mismatch). It fails if the file is smaller than struct fw_header (r8152.c:4655), if the SHA-256 of fw_hdr->version over size-32 bytes differs from fw_hdr->checksum (rtl8152_fw_verify_checksum, 4660), or if a block header would extend past the end of the file (4670). It then walks the blocks from sizeof(*fw_hdr), advancing by ALIGN(block->length, 8). RTL_FW_END must have length == sizeof(struct fw_block) and ends the walk; reaching the end of the file without an END block is not itself an error. PLA and USB blocks must each appear at most once and pass rtl8152_is_fw_mac_ok. PHY_START is rejected if START, any NC/UNION_NC/NC1/NC2/UC2/UC or STOP was already seen, and must have length == sizeof(struct fw_phy_patch_key); PHY_STOP requires START seen and no earlier STOP, with length == sizeof(struct fw_block); PHY_NC and the PHY_UNION_NC/NC1/NC2/UC2/UC blocks require START seen and STOP not seen, are each allowed once, and obey ordering constraints against the later-numbered union kinds, and each passes its rtl8152_is_fw_phy_nc_ok / rtl8152_is_fw_phy_union_ok check; PHY_UNION_MISC only has to pass the union check and may repeat; PHY_FIXUP must pass rtl8152_is_fw_phy_fixup_ok and may repeat; PHY_SPEED_UP is allowed once and must pass rtl8152_is_fw_phy_speed_up_ok; PHY_VER is allowed once, only before any START/NC/UNION/STOP block, and must pass rtl8152_is_fw_phy_ver_ok. Unknown block types only produce a warning and are skipped. After the walk (or at an END block) it fails with -EFAULT if PHY_START was seen but PHY_STOP was not; it does not require PLA, USB or any PHY block to be present. It only reads the firmware and logs; it takes no locks and allocates nothing.

Old prose also omitted that an unknown-type block with length 0 would not advance i (not asserted)

name: usbnet_probe
prose: Generic probe for usbnet-based USB network drivers. First, if the bound usb_driver does not yet support autosuspend it sets supports_autosuspend and calls pm_runtime_enable on the interface (usbnet.c:1720-1723). If prod->driver_info is NULL it returns -ENODEV (no allocation done). It allocates an etherdev (alloc_etherdev failure returns -ENOMEM straight through the out label), initialises the usbnet structure, queues, work items, timer and mutexes, and then either calls info->bind (a negative result goes to out1 without calling unbind), or, when info->in/out are not both set, calls usbnet_get_endpoints, or otherwise sets the in/out pipes from info, calls usb_set_interface unless FLAG_NO_SETINT, and checks the bulk endpoints (-EINVAL on failure). If status is still non-negative and dev->status is set it calls init_status. A negative status at that point goes to out3. It then defaults rx_urb_size, computes maxpacket (zero gives -ENODEV via out4), assigns a random MAC if the address is invalid, sets device types, updates the max queue lengths, and, when can_dma_sg is set without FLAG_SEND_ZLP/FLAG_MULTI_PACKET, allocates a 1-byte padding_pkt (failure: -ENOMEM via out4). register_netdev failure goes to out5. On success it stores dev as interface data, calls netif_device_attach, calls usbnet_link_change(dev,0,0) when FLAG_LINK_INTR is set, and returns 0. Error unwinding falls through: out5 kfree(padding_pkt), out4 usb_free_urb(dev->interrupt), out3 info->unbind if non-NULL, out1 usbnet_mark_going_away, cancel_work_sync(kevent), timer_delete_sync(delay), free_netdev, then out returns status. A failed bind therefore only runs the out1 steps, while any later failure also runs the steps below its label.

name: virtnet_set_hashflow
prose: ethtool set_rxfh_fields handler of virtio_net: changes which RSS hash-type bits are saved for one flow type. Takes no locks. It returns -EINVAL, before changing any state, if info->data is none of exactly (RXH_IP_SRC|RXH_IP_DST), exactly (RXH_IP_SRC|RXH_IP_DST|RXH_L4_B_0_1|RXH_L4_B_2_3) or has the RXH_DISCARD bit set (any value with that bit is accepted), if info->flow_type is not TCP_V4/UDP_V4/IPV4/TCP_V6/UDP_V6/IPV6_FLOW, or if the computed hash types are not a subset of vi->rss_hash_types_supported. Otherwise it starts from vi->rss_hash_types_saved and, for TCP/UDP flows, clears that flow's IPv4 or IPv6 bit and its TCP or UDP bit and, unless RXH_DISCARD is set, sets the IP bit plus the TCP/UDP bit only when the full L4 combination was requested; for IPV4_FLOW/IPV6_FLOW it clears only the IPv4/IPv6 bit and, unless RXH_DISCARD is set, replaces the whole value with just that bit. If the result differs from vi->rss_hash_types_saved it stores it there and in vi->rss_hdr->hash_types (little-endian); then only when NETIF_F_RXHASH is set in vi->dev->features it calls virtnet_commit_rss_command, and if that returns false it returns -EINVAL with the new types already stored. It returns 0 when nothing changed, when changed with NETIF_F_RXHASH clear (no commit), or when the commit succeeds.

name: vmxnet3_probe_device
prose: PCI probe for the vmxnet3 NIC. It sets enable_mq to 0 if MSI is unavailable, picks Tx/Rx queue counts from the number of online CPUs when enable_mq is set (Rx count 1 when RSS support is not compiled in), and allocates the net_device with alloc_etherdev_mq (failure: returns -ENOMEM immediately, with no cleanup). After that pci drvdata is set to the netdev, and it stays set on the failure paths as well. It then, in order: sets a 64-bit DMA mask (on failure it returns that error via err_set_mask); maps the adapter structure for DMA (mapping error: -EFAULT via err_set_mask); allocates the shared structure (-ENOMEM via err_alloc_shared); calls vmxnet3_alloc_pci_resources (negative result returned via err_alloc_pci); negotiates the hardware revision by trying revisions from VMXNET3_REV_9 down to REV_1 and the UPT version through VMXNET3_REG_UVRS (no match or UPT bit 0 clear: -EBUSY via err_ver); for version >= 7 reads the device and passthrough capability registers, writes the device-capability register and issues the GET_DCR0_REG command under cmd_lock, chooses the producer register offsets, determines the queue counts (querying the device when the version is >= 6), allocates the coherent queue-descriptor area (-ENOMEM via err_ver), pm_conf (-ENOMEM via err_alloc_pm), rss_conf if VMXNET3_RSS is compiled in (via err_alloc_rss), and coal_conf for version >= 3 (via err_coal_conf). It then sets up features, interrupt resources (vmxnet3_alloc_intr_resources has no return value that is checked), RSS flag, MAC address, ops, MTU range, the reset work item, NAPI instances, and queue counts, and calls register_netdev; failure there goes to err_register. On success it calls vmxnet3_check_link and returns 0. The err_register path frees coal_conf (version >= 3), then the interrupt resources, and then falls through freeing rss_conf, pm_conf, the queue-descriptor memory, the PCI resources, the shared structure, unmapping the adapter mapping and free_netdev; later labels skip the earlier frees. Note the unwinding is not strictly the reverse of allocation order (coal_conf is freed before the interrupt resources although it was allocated before them).

name: vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf
prose: Fills receive descriptors of one Rx command ring of a vmxnet3 queue, starting at ring->next2fill, and returns the number of descriptors made available to the device (the slice cut the head; the function is vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf(rq, ring_idx, num_to_alloc, adapter)). The loop runs while num_allocated <= num_to_alloc. For each slot it sets comp_state to PENDING and prepares a buffer according to rbi->buf_type: an XDP buffer is taken from the queue's page pool; an skb buffer is allocated with __netdev_alloc_skb_ip_align and DMA-mapped only if rbi->skb is NULL; a page buffer (BUG_ON if the type is not PAGE or len is not PAGE_SIZE) is allocated with alloc_page(GFP_ATOMIC) and DMA-mapped only if rbi->page is NULL. An existing skb or page is reused without remapping. An allocation or DMA-mapping failure (the mapped skb or page is freed first in the mapping-failure cases) increments rq->stats.rx_buf_alloc_failure and stops the loop. The descriptor address, length, buffer type and the inverted generation bit are written; when num_allocated has reached num_to_alloc the slot is marked COMP_DONE and the loop ends without setting the generation bit (the last slot is filled but not handed to the device and next2fill is not advanced); otherwise the generation bit is set, num_allocated is incremented and next2fill is advanced. After the loop it logs, executes BUG_ON(num_allocated != 0 && ring->next2fill == ring->next2comp) and returns num_allocated, which can be 0 on an immediate failure.

name: vrf_ip6_rcv
prose: Receive hook for IPv6 packets arriving on a VRF slave (defined at vrf.c:1323 when CONFIG_IPV6 is enabled; the stub at 1381 for non-IPv6 builds just returns skb). It saves orig_iif = skb->skb_iif and computes need_strict (rt6_need_strict on the destination) and is_ndisc (neighbour-discovery ICMPv6). Branch 1, taken when skb->pkt_type is PACKET_LOOPBACK or (need_strict and not NDISC): sets skb->dev = vrf_dev, skb->skb_iif = vrf_dev->ifindex and IP6SKB_L3SLAVE in IP6CB; if the packet was loopback it sets pkt_type = PACKET_HOST and does no dst lookup, otherwise it calls vrf_ip6_input_dst(skb, vrf_dev, orig_iif); it then returns skb without running netfilter. Otherwise (not loopback and either not strict or NDISC): if the frame is not NDISC it adds vrf_dev rx stats, sets skb->dev and skb->skb_iif to the VRF, taps the packet through dev_queue_xmit_nit when vrf_dev->ptype_all is non-empty and the mac header could be added, and sets IP6SKB_L3SLAVE; an NDISC frame keeps its dev, skb_iif and flags. If need_strict (including strict NDISC) it then calls vrf_ip6_input_dst. Finally it returns vrf_rcv_nfhook(NFPROTO_IPV6, NF_INET_PRE_ROUTING, ...), which is NULL unless nf_hook returned 1 (when NULL the netfilter code has taken over the skb). vrf_ip6_input_dst first drops the skb's existing dst (skb_dst_drop) and sets a new dst only if the VRF-table lookup returns a non-NULL entry that is not the ip6 null entry, so on a failed lookup the skb is left without a dst.

name: vxlan_snoop
prose: Learns or updates the VXLAN FDB entry for a received packet's source (called with RCU read lock held; it uses vxlan_find_mac_rcu). Returns SKB_DROP_REASON_MAC_INVALID_SOURCE with no other effect if src_mac is not a valid unicast Ethernet address (vxlan_core.c:1447). It computes ifindex = src_ifindex only when src_ip is an IPv6 link-local address (CONFIG_IPV6), else 0. If an entry for (src_mac, vni) exists: it writes f->updated = jiffies if it differs; then returns SKB_DROP_REASON_VXLAN_ENTRY_EXISTS if the entry has a nexthop; else returns SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET if the first remote's remote_ip equals *src_ip and its remote_ifindex equals ifindex (this test comes before the static check, so a static entry with the same address also returns NOT_DROPPED_YET); else returns SKB_DROP_REASON_VXLAN_ENTRY_EXISTS if f->state has NUD_PERMANENT or NUD_NOARP; else (migration) it logs under net_ratelimit, sets the first remote's remote_ip = *src_ip (remote_ifindex is not changed), sends an RTM_NEWNEIGH notification and falls through to return SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET. If no entry exists it takes vxlan->hash_lock (spin_lock), and only when netif_running(dev) calls vxlan_fdb_update to create a NUD_REACHABLE entry with NLM_F_EXCL|NLM_F_CREATE (its result is ignored), releases the lock and returns SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET, whether or not an entry was created.

name: vxlan_fdb_update_existing
prose: Applies a netlink add/replace/append request to an existing vxlan FDB entry f (rtnl lock held; uses rtnl_dereference/rcu_access_pointer on f->nh). It first returns -EOPNOTSUPP, with f unchanged, if nhid is non-zero but f has no nexthop, if nhid is non-zero together with NLM_F_APPEND, or if f has a nexthop and state lacks NUD_PERMANENT and NUD_NOARP. Unless the request carries NTF_EXT_LEARNED while f->flags has NTF_VXLAN_ADDED_BY_USER, it copies state into f->state and (ndm_flags & ~NTF_USE) into f->flags, noting a change if either differed. With NLM_F_REPLACE: for a unicast, non-zero key MAC it calls vxlan_fdb_nh_update when nhid is non-zero (a negative result is returned immediately; it returns 0 without change if f already uses that nexthop id, 1 after switching to it taking a reference and dropping the old one, or -EINVAL for an unknown, deleted, non-fdb or non-multipath nexthop, or -EAFNOSUPPORT for a family mismatch with vxlan->default_dst.remote_ip, releasing the reference it took), or else vxlan_fdb_replace, which rewrites the first remote (ip, port, vni, ifindex) unless an identical remote already exists; for a multicast or all-zero key MAC it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. With NLM_F_APPEND and a multicast or all-zero key MAC it calls vxlan_fdb_append, which adds a new remote unless an identical one exists (-ENOMEM if the allocation fails, returned immediately). With NTF_USE it sets f->updated to jiffies. If anything changed it sets f->updated, and calls vxlan_fdb_notify(RTM_NEWNEIGH, swdev_notify) on the appended or else first remote; if the notify fails with a non-zero nhid it returns that error, otherwise it restores the replaced remote (REPLACE) or removes the appended one (APPEND) before returning the error. Otherwise it returns 0. State/flags changes made earlier are not reverted on any error path after they were stored, and without NLM_F_REPLACE/NLM_F_APPEND the remotes are not touched.

name: qmc_hcld_recv_complete
prose: RX-completion callback of the Freescale QMC HDLC driver (the source spells it qmc_hcld_recv_complete, fsl_qmc_hdlc.c:248; the slice cut its head). The context is the qmc_hdlc_desc that was queued for receive. It first unmaps the descriptor's DMA buffer (dma_unmap_single, desc->dma_size). If flags has any QMC_HDLC_RX_ERROR_FLAGS bit it increments rx_errors, plus rx_over_errors for OVF, rx_frame_errors once for UNA and once more for ABORT, and rx_crc_errors for CRC, frees desc->skb and goes to re-queue. Otherwise, with crc_size 4 if is_crc32 else 2, if length < crc_size it increments rx_length_errors, frees the skb and goes to re-queue; else it subtracts the CRC, increments rx_packets, adds the reduced length to rx_bytes, skb_put()s that length, sets skb->protocol with hdlc_type_trans and passes the skb to netif_rx (ownership passes to the stack). In all three paths it then calls qmc_hdlc_recv_queue(qmc_hdlc, desc, desc->dma_size). That call allocates a new skb into desc->skb; if dev_alloc_skb fails desc->skb is NULL and nothing needs freeing; if the DMA mapping or qmc_chan_read_submit fails it unmaps (submit failure only) and frees the new skb and sets desc->skb to NULL. On any non-zero result this callback logs an error and increments rx_errors, and the descriptor is then not queued for receive. The callback returns nothing.

name: raw_eth_ioctl
prose: ioctl handler for the HDLC Ethernet-emulation protocol, switching on ifs->type. IF_GET_PROTO: returns -EINVAL if the device's current HDLC protocol is not this one; otherwise sets ifs->type to IF_PROTO_HDLC_ETH, and if ifs->size is smaller than sizeof(raw_hdlc_proto) sets ifs->size to that size and returns -ENOBUFS; else copies the protocol state (hdlc->state) to the user buffer, returning -EFAULT if the copy fails and 0 otherwise. IF_PROTO_HDLC_ETH: returns -EPERM without CAP_NET_ADMIN, -EBUSY if IFF_UP is set, -EFAULT if the settings cannot be copied from user space; it replaces ENCODING_DEFAULT with ENCODING_NRZ and PARITY_DEFAULT with PARITY_CRC16_PR1_CCITT, then calls hdlc->attach(dev, encoding, parity) and returns its result if non-zero, then attach_hdlc_protocol(dev, &proto, sizeof(raw_hdlc_proto)) and returns its result if non-zero. attach_hdlc_protocol first calls detach_hdlc_protocol, which on success drops the previous protocol, frees its state and resets the device; if that detach fails (for example a netdev notifier refuses NETDEV_PRE_TYPE_CHANGE) the previous protocol stays; after a successful detach it can still fail with -ENOSYS (module reference) or -ENOBUFS (state allocation), leaving no protocol attached. On success it copies the new settings into hdlc->state, runs ether_setup while keeping tx_queue_len, clears IFF_TX_SKB_SHARING, assigns a random hardware address, sends NETDEV_POST_TYPE_CHANGE, calls netif_dormant_off and returns 0. Any other ifs->type returns -EINVAL with no side effects.

name: n2_run
prose: Probes and registers one RISCom/N2 card (n2.c:321, __init). Arguments io, irq and winbase are range-checked first and the function returns -ENODEV, with nothing allocated and without calling n2_destroy_card, if io is outside 0x200-0x3FF or not a multiple of N2_IOPORTS, if irq is outside 3-15 or equals 6, or if winbase is outside 0xA0000-0xFFFFF or not 4 KiB aligned. It then allocates a zeroed card_t (failure: -ENOBUFS, nothing to release and no n2_destroy_card call). Every later failure calls n2_destroy_card(card) and returns: -ENOMEM if either hdlc net device allocation fails; -EBUSY if request_region, request_irq or request_mem_region fails; -EFAULT if ioremap fails; -ENODEV if USE_WINDOWSIZE is not 16384, 32768 or 65536; -EIO if the RAM test leaves tx_ring_buffers below 1; -ENOBUFS if register_hdlc_device fails for a port (that port's card pointer is cleared first so n2_destroy_card does not unregister it, ports already registered are unregistered). n2_destroy_card releases the IRQ, I/O region, ioremap and memory region only when card->irq, card->io or card->winbase respectively are set; because card->winbase is NULL after a failed ioremap, the memory region from request_mem_region is not released on the -EFAULT path. The function divides by (valid0 + valid1) when sizing the rings, so callers must pass at least one non-zero valid flag. On success it programs the PCR/BAR/PSR registers, sizes the RAM, computes the TX/RX ring counts, starts the SCA, initialises and registers an hdlc device for each enabled port, stores the card in *new_card, advances new_card to &card->next_card and returns 0.

name: n2_init
prose: Module init for the N2 driver (n2.c:476, __init). If the module parameter string hw is NULL it returns -EINVAL (after logging 'no card initialized' only when built as a module). Otherwise it prints the version and parses hw, advancing the global hw pointer, as a sequence of specifications io,irq,ram,ports separated by ':' where ports is a run of the characters '0' and '1' (each at most once). A missing comma after io, irq or ram ends the loop (break), as does a specification that enables neither port. For a specification that enabled at least one port and is followed by ':' or the end of the string it calls n2_run(io, irq, ram, valid[0], valid[1]) and ignores its return value, so n2_run errors are not propagated. If the string ends right after a specification it returns first_card ? 0 : -EINVAL immediately, without printing the error. When the loop is left in any other way (break, or the character after the specification is neither ':' nor NUL) it logs 'invalid hardware parameters' and returns first_card ? 0 : -EINVAL. first_card is non-NULL only if some earlier n2_run call succeeded, so the function returns 0 whenever at least one card was registered, even if a later specification was malformed or failed. An n2_run failure on the ioremap path leaves its memory region requested.

name: ath10k_bmi_set_start
prose: Sends a BMI set-application-start command to the target. The listed name bmi_set_app_start does not exist; the function in bmi.c:501 is ath10k_bmi_set_start(ar, address). It builds the command locally (cmd.id = BMI_SET_APP_START, little-endian, and the address) so the caller supplies no command buffer. If ar->bmi.done_sent is already set it logs a warning and returns -EBUSY without sending anything. Otherwise it calls ath10k_hif_exchange_bmi_msg(ar, &cmd, cmdlen, NULL, NULL) with cmdlen = sizeof(cmd.id) + sizeof(cmd.set_app_start); if that returns non-zero it logs a warning and returns that value; otherwise it returns 0. It takes no locks itself and does not modify ar->bmi.

name: ath10k_core_fetch_firmware_api_n
prose: Loads an ath10k 'firmware-N.bin' file by name and parses its IE (information element) list into *fw_file. It calls ath10k_fetch_fw_file(ar, ar->hw_params.fw.dir, name) and stores the result in fw_file->firmware; if that is an error pointer it returns the negative errno (the error pointer stays in fw_file->firmware, nothing is released). Otherwise it returns -EINVAL if the file is shorter than the magic string (including its NUL), if the magic does not match, or if an IE's declared length exceeds the remaining data; in these cases it goes to err, which calls ath10k_core_free_firmware_files(ar) (this releases the firmware files held in ar, namely ar->normal_mode_fw.fw_file.firmware, the cal and pre-cal files and the code-swap segments, rather than naming the fw_file argument). name: ath10k_sdio_mbox_rxmsg_pending_handler

name: ath11k_mac_update_vif_chan

name: ath12k_dp_tx
prose: Enqueues one 802.11 data frame on a TCL ring (ath12k dp_tx.c:222; the slice cut the head). If none is available it counts desc_na, sets ret = -ENOMEM and, only if not all rings have been tried (ring_map) and hw_params->tcl_ring_retry is set, increments ring_selector and sets tcl_ring_retry. Every failure after the tx descriptor was assigned unwinds as applicable (ext-desc unmap, free ext skb, unmap data, ath12k_dp_tx_release_txbuf) and increments arvif->link_stats.tx_dropped; the retry jump back to tcl_ring_sel happens only after the TCL-ring-full failure, not for DMA, ext-skb, HTT-metadata, encap or alignment failures, which return their error. On success it updates link and device statistics, writes the TCL descriptor, increments ar->dp.num_tx_pending and returns 0, with the skb recorded in tx_desc->skb for the completion path. The skb may have been modified in place (nwifi encap, MIC length added, realignment); on failure the function does not free the skb.

name: ath12k_htc_connect_service
prose: Connects an HTC service to an endpoint (ath12k htc.c:557; the slice cut the head). name: ath12k_peer_assoc_h_he
prose: Fills the HE (802.11ax) fields of a WMI peer-assoc argument (ath12k mac.c:2447; the slice cut the head). It returns without writing to arg when the vif link channel lookup fails (WARN_ON), when the link bss conf or the link sta cannot be obtained (warning), when the peer has no HE capability, or when every entry of arvif->bitrate_mask.control[band].he_mcs is zero (ath12k_peer_assoc_h_he_masked returns true only when all entries are zero; a mask with any non-zero entry lets processing continue). If the mask's highest NSS exceeds link_sta->rx_nss and no mask entry at or below rx_nss - 1 is non-zero, it overwrites he_mcs_mask[rx_nss - 1] (the caller's bitrate mask) with the highest entry. It then stores the rx/tx HE MCS-NSS maps for 80 MHz and, when link_sta->bandwidth is 160 MHz, for 160 MHz too (peer_he_mcs_count counts the sets written) and computes arg->peer_nss from the maximum NSS (limited by ar->num_tx_chains and link_sta->rx_nss). name: ath12k_mac_get_rate_hw_value
prose: Returns the WMI fixed-rate code for a legacy bitrate in units of 100 kbit/s (mac.c:3763). It classifies the bitrate as CCK (10, 20, 55, 110 selects preamble WMI_RATE_PREAMBLE_CCK = 1) or otherwise OFDM (preamble 0), then looks the bitrate up in the ath12k_legacy_rates table; on a match it returns ATH12K_HW_RATE_CODE(hw_value, 0, preamble) = (1 << 28) | (preamble << 8) | hw_value, with hw_value taken from the table (CCK long-preamble 11M=0, 5.5M=1, 2M=2, 1M=3; OFDM 48M=0, 24M=1, 12M=2, 6M=3, 54M=4, 36M=5, 18M=6, 9M=7). So for example 10 gives 0x10000103, 110 gives 0x10000100, 60 gives 0x10000003, 540 gives 0x10000004. If the bitrate matches none of 10, 20, 55, 110, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 360, 480, 540 it returns -EINVAL converted to u32 (4294967274). It reads the static rate table and has no side effects.

name: ath12k_mac_vdev_create
prose: Creates a firmware vdev for a link vif and registers it on ar (ath12k mac.c:9677; the slice cut the head; caller holds the wiphy mutex). It returns, with no state modified, -EINVAL if vif is a monitor interface and ar->monitor_vdev_created is set, -ENOSPC if ar->num_created_vdevs has reached TARGET_NUM_VDEVS, and -ENOLINK if link_id is below IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS but the link conf is NULL. After a successful vdev creation it increments ar->num_created_vdevs, sets is_created, updates allocated_vdev_map and free_vdev_map, adds arvif to ar->arvifs under data_lock, and sets the NSS param. Failure of that param goes to err_vdev_del. By vdev type: AP creates a peer (failure: err_vdev_del) and sets kickout parameters (failure: err_peer_del); STA sets four power-save settings (failure: err_peer_del) and may prepare the 11d scan state; MONITOR sets ar->monitor_vdev_created. name: ath12k_mac_assign_vif_to_vdev

name: ath5k_hw_phy_init
prose: Initialises the ath5k PHY during reset, or performs a fast channel change (phy.c:3741-3952; the slice shows only the tail, the function is ath5k_hw_phy_init(ah, channel, mode, fast); it assumes the PHY is in warm reset). It returns -EINVAL if fast is set and channel->hw_value differs from the current channel's hw_value. When fast it requests the RF bus and polls up to 100 times (5 us apart) for the grant (-EIO if not granted), sets the channel with ath5k_hw_channel (error returned) and waits for the synthesizer. Next, for all callers, it sets TX power with ath5k_hw_txpower (error returned) and, on AR5212 for channels whose hw_value is not AR5K_MODE_11B, writes the OFDM timings (error returned) and, if the MAC revision is at least AR5424, sets the spur mitigation filter. If fast it then releases the RF bus request, starts noise-floor calibration (AGCCTL_NF) and returns 0. When not fast: for chips other than AR5210 it initialises RF gain and RF registers (each error returned) and sets or clears the 5111 B-mode bit in TXCFG; for AR5210 it only disables the PHY with delays; then it sets the channel (error returned), enables the PHY, waits for the synthesizer, runs a bounded ADC-test wait (no error reported), starts AGC and noise-floor calibration, starts I/Q calibration unless mode is AR5K_MODE_11B (setting ah->ah_iq_cal_needed accordingly), waits for AGC calibration to finish (a timeout is only logged, not returned), restores the antenna mode and returns 0.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers (name not in slice): the slice is the tail of ath5k_hw_phy_init (phy.c:3741-3952), fixed under that name; old prose said 'gain-calibration timeout only reported' which is right

name: ath5k_hw_setup_tx_queue
prose: Allocates and sets up an ath5k TX queue of the given type and returns its index (qcu.c:202). The queue number depends on the hardware: if cap_queues.q_tx_num is 2, DATA maps to AR5K_TX_QUEUE_ID_NOQCU_DATA, BEACON and CAB to AR5K_TX_QUEUE_ID_NOQCU_BEACON and any other type returns -EINVAL; otherwise DATA uses queue_info->tqi_subtype as the index (queue_info is dereferenced here, so it must be non-NULL for DATA, and the index is not range-checked), UAPSD, BEACON and CAB use their fixed ids, and other types return -EINVAL. It then zeroes ah->ah_txq[queue] and sets its tqi_type to queue_type (before any bounds check). If queue_info is non-NULL it sets queue_info->tqi_type = queue_type and calls ath5k_hw_set_tx_queueprops; a non-zero return (that function returns -EIO if the entry is AR5K_TX_QUEUE_INACTIVE) is returned unchanged, after the entry has already been cleared. Note ath5k_hw_set_tx_queueprops returns false (0) when the queue index is not below q_tx_num, so an out-of-range index does not produce an error here. Finally it enables the queue's bit in ah_txq_status and returns the queue index.

name: ath5k_hw_reset
prose: Main (re)initialisation function of the ath5k hardware (reset.c:1145-1380; the slice cut the head): ath5k_hw_reset(ah, op_mode, channel, fast, skip_pcu). Fast channel change is kept only when ah->ah_radio is AR5K_RF2413 or AR5K_RF5413, otherwise fast is cleared. On AR5212 it then writes the hardware (ath5k_hw_set_sleep_clock(ah, false)) before validating the channel. It returns -EINVAL, logging an error, if channel->hw_value is not 11A, 11G or 11B, is 11G on AR5210/AR5211, or is 11B on AR5210. If fast is set it calls ath5k_hw_phy_init(..., true): on success it returns 0 immediately; on failure it falls back to the full reset (the error is not returned). The full reset saves the frame sequence counters (all 10 DCU counters before AR5211, DCU 0 only after), the TSF on AR5211 and the LED/GPIO state, runs gain calibration on AR5212 with RF <= 5112 when !fast and RF banks exist, then calls ath5k_hw_nic_wakeup (error returned), enables PHY access, calls ath5k_hw_write_initvals(ah, mode, skip_pcu) (error returned), initialises the core clock, tweaks initvals, commits EEPROM settings, restores the saved sequence/TSF/LED/GPIO values, calls ath5k_hw_pcu_init(ah, op_mode), ath5k_hw_phy_init(..., false) (error returned) and ath5k_hw_init_queues (error returned), then initialises DMA. On AR5212 with ah_use_32khz_clock and op_mode other than AP it enables the 32 kHz sleep clock. Finally it disables beacons, resets the TSF and returns 0. op_mode is only used by ath5k_hw_pcu_init and the 32 kHz decision; it is not validated. On the failure returns after the hardware was touched, earlier register writes are not undone.

name: ath5k_hw_commit_eeprom_settings
prose: Static helper in ath5k reset.c (975-1123; the slice shows only its tail) that programs PHY registers from the EEPROM data for the channel. It returns immediately for AR5210 (no EEPROM support). Otherwise it derives ee_mode from the channel, computes the CCK/OFDM power delta (using the scaled CCK delta for channel 14, 2484 MHz), and on PHY revisions from AR5212A writes AR5K_PHY_TX_PWR_ADJ (the negated gain delta and power delta for 11G channels, 0 otherwise) while on older revisions it stores the deltas in ah->ah_txpower for software scaling. It then sets the antenna switch for ee_mode, writes the noise-floor threshold, and, if the bandwidth mode is 40 MHz and the EEPROM version is at least 5.0, writes the turbo variants of switch settling, TX/RX attenuation, ADC/PGA desired size and TX/RX margin; otherwise it writes the normal variants (the TX/RX margin only for EEPROM version >= 4.1). It then writes the XPA delays, XLNA delay, the ANI threshold and the cyclic-power RSSI threshold (with the EEPROM false-detect backoff added if the channel has spur noise), for EEPROM version >= 4.0 the I/Q correction values and its enable bit, and for version >= 5.1 clears the heavy-clipping enable register. It returns nothing and takes no locks.

name: SIMPLE_SHOW_STORE(ani_mode, ah->ani_state.ani_mode, ath5k_ani_init)
prose: Generated function ath5k_attr_show_ani_mode (from the SIMPLE_SHOW_STORE macro in ath5k sysfs.c) is the sysfs show callback for the 'ani_mode' attribute. It takes the ieee80211_hw from dev_get_drvdata(dev), ah = hw->priv, and returns sysfs_emit(buf, "%d\n", ah->ani_state.ani_mode), that is the current ANI mode as a decimal integer with a newline written into buf, and the number of characters written. It does not modify any state and takes no locks of its own; dev must have drvdata set to a valid ieee80211_hw whose priv is an ath5k_hw.

name: ath6kl_htc_mbox_conn_service
prose: Connects an HTC service and configures its endpoint (ath6kl htc_mbox.c:2420; the slice cut the head). For the pseudo control service HTC_CTRL_RSVD_SVC it uses ENDPOINT_0 with max message size HTC_MAX_CTRL_MSG_LEN and sends nothing (conn_resp->resp_code is not written). Otherwise it takes a control tx buffer (-ENOMEM if none), builds and issues a connect-service message with ath6kl_htc_tx_issue (a non-zero status is returned), waits for the response control packet (-ENOMEM if none arrives), and returns -ENOMEM if the message id is wrong or the response is too short; it then copies the response status to conn_resp->resp_code and returns -ENOMEM if the status is not HTC_SERVICE_SUCCESS, otherwise it takes the assigned endpoint and max message size from the response. Common part: -ENOMEM if the endpoint is ENDPOINT_UNUSED or >= ENDPOINT_MAX or max_msg_sz is 0 (before anything is written); it then writes endpoint->eid and returns -ENOMEM if endpoint->svc_id is already set (conn_resp is not yet written at that point, though resp_code may have been). Otherwise it sets conn_resp->endpoint and ->len_max, marks the endpoint in use by setting svc_id, then max_txq_depth, len_max, ep_cb, the cred_dist fields, and tx_drop_packet_threshold (MAX_DEF_COOKIE_NUM / 3 for WMI_DATA_BK_SVC, else MAX_HI_COOKIE_NUM). If conn_req->max_rxmsg_sz is non-zero and larger than max_msg_sz it returns -ENOMEM at that point, leaving the endpoint marked in use with cred_per_msg and conn_flags not set; otherwise cred_per_msg is max_rxmsg_sz (or max_msg_sz) divided by target->tgt_cred_sz (which must be non-zero), raised to at least 1, and conn_flags is set from conn_req->flags and the function returns 0. On every path after the buffers were taken (success or failure) the tx control buffer is reclaimed and the rx packet, if any, is reset and returned; the function takes no locks itself. Many non-memory failures are reported as -ENOMEM.
